name: AdGuard Home
description: Network-wide ad and tracker blocking DNS server.
about: Filters DNS queries to block ads and trackers. Configure your router or individual devices to use this server.

variables.label: Config folder
variables.description: Holds AdGuardHome.yaml, which has every setting, blocklist, client, and the admin account. Losing it drops you back to the setup wizard, so back it up.

variables.label: Data folder
variables.description: Downloaded blocklists, the query log, and statistics. Has to be a different folder from the config one.

variables.label: DNS port
variables.description: DNS queries use TCP and UDP, normally on port 53. If systemd-resolved or another service already uses that port, free it or choose a port your clients support.

variables.label: Dashboard port
variables.description: Host port for the dashboard and setup wizard. Keep the wizard on all interfaces and container port 3000. If access is lost, stop the container and correct http.address in AdGuardHome.yaml.

variables.label: Publish DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-QUIC
variables.description: Opens host port 853 so clients can query over an encrypted connection. Nothing answers there until you add a certificate under Settings, Encryption.

variables.label: Publish HTTPS and DNS-over-HTTPS
variables.description: Opens host port 443 for the HTTPS dashboard and DNS-over-HTTPS. Nothing answers there until you add a certificate under Settings, Encryption. The UDP half only carries traffic once you also turn on HTTP/3.

variables.label: Publish DNSCrypt
variables.description: Opens host port 5443 for DNSCrypt clients. There is no dashboard page for it. Nothing answers there until you set port_dnscrypt and dnscrypt_config_file in the tls section of AdGuardHome.yaml.

variables.label: Timezone
variables.description: IANA name such as Europe/London. Sets the timestamps in the container's log output. The query log renders in your browser's timezone regardless.
